questions.question: What HTTP method submits data to be processed?
questions.explanation: POST sends data to the server to create or update resources.

questions.question: What HTTP method updates an existing resource?
questions.explanation: PUT replaces the entire resource with the provided data.

questions.question: What HTTP method partially updates a resource?
questions.explanation: PATCH applies partial modifications to a resource.

questions.question: What HTTP method deletes a resource?
questions.explanation: DELETE removes the specified resource from the server.

questions.question: What secure alternative to FTP uses SSL/TLS?
questions.explanation: FTPS adds SSL/TLS encryption to standard FTP connections.

questions.question: What DNS record type maps domain names to IPv4 addresses?
questions.explanation: A records map hostnames to 32-bit IPv4 addresses.

questions.question: What DNS record type maps domain names to IPv6 addresses?
questions.explanation: AAAA records map hostnames to 128-bit IPv6 addresses.

questions.question: What DHCP message does a client send to discover servers?
questions.explanation: DHCPDISCOVER broadcasts to locate available DHCP servers.

questions.question: What DHCP message does a client send to request an IP address?
questions.explanation: DHCPREQUEST asks a specific server to assign an IP address.

questions.question: What protocol version adds encryption and authentication to SNMP?
questions.explanation: SNMPv3 adds security features including authentication and encryption.

questions.question: What DNS record type specifies the mail servers for a domain?
questions.explanation: MX records direct email to a domain's designated mail servers.

questions.question: What DNS record type maps an IP address back to a hostname?
questions.explanation: PTR records enable reverse DNS lookups from IP addresses to names.

questions.question: What DHCP message does a server send to acknowledge and finalize a lease?
questions.explanation: DHCPACK completes the DORA process, confirming the IP address assignment.

questions.question: What HTTP status code indicates the client is forbidden from accessing a resource?
questions.explanation: HTTP 403 means the server understood the request but refuses to authorize it.

questions.question: What transport protocol does HTTP/3 use instead of TCP?
questions.explanation: HTTP/3 runs over QUIC, a UDP-based transport with built-in encryption and lower latency.

questions.question: An HTTP response is returned to a client carrying status code 206 after a Range request. What does this status code indicate?
alternatives: the server is returning only part of the resource
questions.explanation: 206 Partial Content means the server is fulfilling a Range request by returning only the requested byte range of the resource.

questions.question: A packet capture shows a host broadcasting from 0.0.0.0 port 68 to 255.255.255.255 port 67 right after booting. Which protocol is the client using?
questions.explanation: A DHCP client with no address sends DHCPDISCOVER from 0.0.0.0:68 to the broadcast address on UDP port 67 where the server listens.

questions.question: Before trusting a website's certificate, a browser queries the CA in real time to check whether the certificate has been revoked. Which protocol is it using?
questions.explanation: OCSP (Online Certificate Status Protocol) provides real-time certificate revocation status checks, an alternative to downloading CRLs.

questions.question: An administrator wants www.example.com to point to web01.example.com so the web server's name can change without updating users. Which DNS record type creates this alias?
questions.explanation: A CNAME (canonical name) record maps an alias hostname to another hostname rather than to an IP address.

questions.question: An FTP session stalls because the client's firewall blocks the server's inbound data connection. In which FTP mode does the server initiate the data connection back to the client?
questions.explanation: In active-mode FTP the client sends a PORT command and the server opens the data connection back; in passive mode the client initiates both connections.
